"Create a top-down 2D action RPG with strong exploration and freedom, inspired by classic games like Exiled Kingdoms and Kingdoms Two Crowns.
Core concept:
A single-player open-world style game set on a large, diverse island filled with different biomes: dense overgrown forests, murky swamps, ruined towns, caves, crypts, and abandoned villages. The player is a lone adventurer who can freely explore, fight with magic and weapons, complete quests, manage NPCs, and grow stronger.
Perspective @COMMENT_BODY@ Art Style:
Strictly top-down (bird’s-eye view), 2D pixel art.
The color palette should be dominated by sickly, moldy greens mixed with dusty yellows and muted ochres — like a late afternoon in an abandoned, overgrown place similar to Chernobyl. Vegetation should look slightly unhealthy and overgrown, with a yellowish, desaturated light. Avoid pure dark fantasy black/purple tones. The world should feel lived-in, decaying and atmospheric, with animated vegetation and subtle weather effects (fog, light rain, dust).
Gameplay systems:
Free exploration of a large connected map with hidden areas, secret chests, and points of interest.
Real-time combat focused on magic and freedom. The player can use different spells and weapons to fight enemies in a fluid, aggressive style.
Character progression: No fixed classes. The player distributes attribute points (Strength, Endurance, Vitality). These attributes influence combat power, survivability, and carrying capacity.
Mana system: The player has a normal mana pool used for spells. There is also an alternative path of divine power. By interacting with churches, praying, completing pilgrimages, and doing charity missions (helping the poor, distributing food, etc.), the player can gain divine power and unlock priest-like abilities.
NPC management system: Instead of gathering and crafting resources manually, the player can assign NPCs to work. The player can build structures such as forges, magic towers, farms, and workshops, then order NPCs to produce weapons, armor, magical items, or other resources.
Inventory system: Inventory is weight-based and limited by the player’s Strength attribute. The player can buy a magical bag that provides infinite space and reduces the effective weight of all carried items to only 10% (example: 100 kg feels like only 10 kg).
Quests: Main story + many side quests given by NPCs. Quests should encourage exploration and interaction with the world.
Optional mercenaries or companions that can be hired to fight alongside the player.
Loot-driven progression with different item rarities (normal, rare, unique, legendary).
Tone @COMMENT_BODY@ Feel:
The game should feel free and empowering. The player should be able to roam the world casting spells and fighting, while also managing NPCs and building structures to support their power. Exploration and combat should be the main focus, with a clear main story available for those who want to follow it.
Additional notes:
Single-player only.
Focus on offline-friendly design.
Combat should feel fluid and satisfying, with good feedback on spells and attacks.
The world should feel dangerous but fair.
Make the game deep enough for 20–40 hours of content with good replayability through different builds, divine path choices, and exploration. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

## Objective
- Finish the playable, mobile-friendly offline RPG “Hollowmere — The Long Dusk” in the existing browser-game project.

## Requirements
- Preserve the island RPG scope: exploration, real-time combat, progression, quests, divine abilities, inventory, settlement, and touch controls.
- Avoid clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation self-contained in HTML, CSS, canvas, and localStorage.
- Use `hollowmere-save` for saves; main quest states are `bell`, `crypt`, `return`, and `done`.

### Completed
- Built the responsive game shell, HUD, journal/map/intro elements, touch-control layout, and visual theme.
- Rebuilt `game.js` with game state, canvas rendering, exploration, enemies, combat, quests, inventory, progression, settlement, map, and keyboard/touch event wiring.
- `node --check game.js` completed without errors.

### Blocked

## Next Move
1. Open the running game in Playwright and check browser console/runtime errors.
2. Test movement, combat, interaction, quest progression, panels, map, and touch controls; fix issues found.
3. Capture and inspect a screenshot, then summarize assumptions and verification.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: game logic, rendering, quests, combat, panels, and controls.
- `index.html`: game UI elements and IDs.
- `style.css`: visual theme and responsive layout.
- `start.sh`: project startup command.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are currently untracked.
- Browser verification and screenshot review remain pending.

## Objective
- Finish and verify the playable, mobile-friendly offline RPG “Hollowmere — The Long Dusk” in the existing browser-game project.

## Requirements
- Preserve the island RPG scope: exploration, real-time combat, progression, quests, divine abilities, inventory, settlement, and touch controls.
- Avoid clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation self-contained in HTML, CSS, canvas, and localStorage.
- Use `hollowmere-save` for saves; main quest states are `bell`, `crypt`, `return`, and `done`.
